business_scope.primary_industry_name: Customs Clearance Brokerage and Bonded Transit Management

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended in 2015)
France-China Investment Protection Treaty (2004) and Double Taxation Agreement (1984, as amended)
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (entered into force 1 February 2019)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisional application 21 September 2017)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (for France, entered into force 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 to L561-50 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Article L561-2-2 and Articles R561-57 to R561-66 of the Commercial Code (Code de commerce); Decree No. 2016-1639 of 29 November 2016 on the register of beneficial owners; transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: True certified copy of passport (UBO / natural person shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notary in the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (corporate shareholder only)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar / Chamber of Commerce in the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) addressed to the French notary and formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (foreign equivalent of casier judiciaire) for the proposed SARL manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial records authority of the gérant's country of nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's confirmation of identity and source of funds for the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate or private bank where the capital contribution is held

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the French CFT/PEP list maintained by Tracfin (ACPR), the European Commission consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN list for USD-based transactions, in accordance with Articles L561-10 and L561-11 of the French Monetary and Financial Code; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, cross-border correspondent relations, and high-risk third countries.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) and the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin characters; names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Cyrillic, Chinese, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin script. The name must be distinctive, not misleading as to the business object, and must not contain prohibited terms without prior ministerial or professional licensing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, file a written recours gracieux with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of notification; if the rejection is confirmed, file a référé before the President of the Commercial Tribunal under Article R123-58 of the Commercial Code. The applicant may also amend the proposed name and submit a fresh availability certificate; no formal extension of the 30-day reservation window exists. Legal counsel may present supplementary trademark search results or a written authorization for sensitive terms to the registry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional: a SARL may domicile its registered office at the manager's home or with a licensed domiciliation company (Articles L123-11-1 and L123-11-2 of the Commercial Code), but a licensed customs brokerage house must maintain physical operational premises in France for DGDDI inspections and Customs record-keeping. A purely virtual office without any operational presence is not permissible for the customs brokerage licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% probability of unannounced DGDDI on-site inspection within the first 18 months of operation; 90%+ for bonded transit or excise-sensitive customs flows.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and negative certificate (recherche de disponibilité de nom)
Drafting of the SARL articles of association (statuts) by a French-qualified corporate counsel or notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed fee or hourly at €250–500/hour)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication of shareholder KYC bundles and signing of the pre-incorporation process
Legal publication of the incorporation announcement (annonce légale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved legal publication journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customs brokerage licence application and operational set-up (agrément de commissionnaire en douane / customs representation declarations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC due diligence, PEP/Sanctions screening and UBO declaration archive (including French Tracfin report preparation)
Apostille / consular legalization of five international public documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Bureau des Légalisations of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs or the competent foreign ministry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations of non-French documents (passports, certificates, bank letters, power of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-appointed expert tariff / prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: General expense fund: corporate seals, notarial miscellanies, filing postage, governance minutes

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, Book II, Title II (Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq.); Décret n°2007-431 of 25 March 2007; EU Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 (Union Customs Code), Article 18, for customs representative authorization; Code des douanes national for brokerage activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI, coordinating registration with the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce / Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier unique de déclaration de création d'entreprise (formerly Formulaire M0) filed electronically at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a SARL (Code de commerce, Article L.223-2); capital may be EUR 1 but must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited in a French bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and held under a blocking certificate until RCS registration. For customs brokerage activity, adequate financial standing and professional civil liability cover are required by the customs authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a constituent meeting of the subscribers held at the registered office, the following resolutions were adopted: (1) The articles of association are adopted in the form of a SARL under the Code de commerce. (2) The share capital is subscribed in full and deposited in accordance with Article L.223-7. (3) The registered office is fixed at the address stated in the articles. (4) [Name] is appointed as Gérant for the company's duration, with powers to act in the corporate name and to apply for the customs representative registration before the DGDDI. (5) The Gérant is authorized to open bank accounts, execute pre-incorporation contracts, and complete the RCS filing. All declarations are made in accordance with law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI RCS national database and Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the RCS national index via infogreffe or INPI to ensure the proposed corporate name is available and not confusingly similar to an existing entity. Verify that the intended registered office address is physically usable and that the proposed activity code NAF 5229B is consistent with customs brokerage. Record the search results before drafting the articles.
required_dossiers: Proposed activity description and ISIC/NAF code
Identity document of the future manager and shareholders
Proof or draft lease of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is challenged or found identical, select an alternative name or obtain a written consent letter from the prior right holder and resubmit the name verification request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, if applicable, a French notaire for contributions in kind or real property
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French setting out corporate form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, manager appointment, share transfer restrictions, and decision-making rules. Execute the statuts before the shareholders and obtain the manager's written acceptance. If contributions in kind are made, have a commissaire aux apports prepare a valuation report.
required_dossiers: List of subscribers with number of shares subscribed
Contribution valuation report, if non-cash contribution
Passport or ID copies of all signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or a third party queries the articles, amend the defective provisions and re-execute the statuts. If the in-kind contribution valuation is challenged, apply to the tribunal de commerce for appointment of a court-appointed appraiser.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital and issuance of blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the SARL in formation. Deposit the full amount of cash contributions and obtain a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) stating the depositary, the amount, and the depositors. Retain this certificate for the incorporation filing; funds are released only upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Identity and KYC documents of subscribers
Proof of source of funds, if requested by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank returns an incomplete block certificate, ask for an amended certificate. If the bank refuses the deposit, choose another regulated French credit institution and re-perform the deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation dossier with the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an account on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, select SARL creation, complete the dynamic M0 declaration, attach all statutory supporting documents, pay the applicable greffe fee, and submit. The Guichet unique transmits the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce for RCS registration. After registration, address DGDDI separately for the customs representative enrollment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the filer receives a formal mise en demeure; submit the missing document or rectification through the Guichet unique within the specified period. If the registration is refused, petition the supervising judge of the register (juge commis au registre) or the tribunal de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of RCS registration and legal publicity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Greffe issues the K-bis extract, allocates the RCS number and SIRET, and records the company in the registers. Verify all particulars in the K-bis, obtain the official legal publication notice if required for third-party effectiveness, and retrieve the company's definitive identification numbers.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate issued by the Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed or contains errors, submit a rectification request to the Greffe and, if necessary, apply to the supervising judge for an order to issue a corrected extract.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; DREAL for environmental site-specific matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Enregistrement en qualité de représentant en douane (RDE) under Article 18 of the Union Customs Code and the French Code des douanes; optionally, Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) certification for enhanced customs facilitation and bonded transit operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), acting for the Ministère de la Transition écologique
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (non-ICPE) for pure customs clearance brokerage offices; site-specific registration or declaration under the ICPE regime is triggered only if bonded transit management includes warehousing, storage, or handling of goods exceeding the environmental rubrique thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For pure brokerage premises: no industrial effluent or VOC emission sources; municipal wastewater connection must comply with local discharge limits. For any bonded or transit warehouse space: comply with EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive 91/271/EEC and French Code de l'environnement, Article R.214-1; air emission thresholds under Directive (EU) 2016/2284; waste handling by licensed carriers with bordereau de suivi des déchets; hazardous goods storage must provide fire-water containment and leak-proof flooring.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain attestation by the commission de sécurité where premises are open to the public, otherwise perform an office fire-safety compliance inspection of means of egress, extinguishers, and fire alarms. Structural load inspection for any bonded storage area by a certified inspection body. Electrical installation certification in accordance with NFC 15-100. Occupational health: draft the DUERP risk assessment, register the workplace with the local town hall, arrange medical clearance for employees, and maintain emergency procedures and drills.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the impots.gouv.fr business portal; customs and EORI registration are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through the French customs online services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is registered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The filing normally includes the articles of association, registered office evidence, director identification, beneficial-owner information, business activity description, and supporting documents for any regulated activity. The formalities authority transmits the data to the Registre national des entreprises, DGFiP, and other competent bodies. The entity receives a SIREN and establishment-level SIRET identifiers. DGFiP assigns or confirms the tax account and French VAT identification number, generally composed of the prefix FR, a two-digit control key, and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity making taxable supplies in France must register with the appropriate SIE; an EU-established entity may generally register directly, while a non-EU entity may need a French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement or statutory exception applies. Customs activities require an EORI number obtained from DGDDI and, where the entity acts as a customs representative, the relevant customs authorizations, representation mandates, and electronic customs-access credentials.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A qualifying SARL, including certain newly formed companies and qualifying family SARLs, may elect for partnership-style income taxation under the statutory conditions and within the applicable election period. The family SARL election can remain available while the statutory family-ownership conditions continue to be met; the temporary new-company election is generally limited in duration. There is no general United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework and can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or apply other consequences to hybrid arrangements; they do not provide a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), supplemented by customs import VAT and excise regimes administered in relevant cases by DGDDI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For domestic French establishments eligible for the VAT franchise regime, the principal annual turnover threshold is generally EUR 25,000, with a tolerance threshold generally up to EUR 27,500 under the applicable current rules. The thresholds vary by activity and are subject to legislative change. A foreign business making taxable supplies in France may have a VAT registration obligation without relying on the domestic small-business threshold, including where it is not eligible for the franchise regime. Import VAT, intra-Community acquisitions, and certain reverse-charge transactions may create reporting obligations independently of the turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for all private-sector transactions. Businesses must issue VAT-compliant invoices and retain reliable electronic records. The French B2B e-invoicing reform requires electronic invoice receipt capability for all businesses from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations apply from 1 September 2026 to large and mid-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 to small and micro-enterprises, subject to the statutory implementation timetable. Transactions within scope will generally be transmitted through an approved private electronic invoicing platform or the public invoicing portal framework, with e-reporting for certain cross-border and consumer transactions. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Customs declarations and customs data are filed electronically through DGDDI systems, with MRN and electronic release or exit records serving as principal customs evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union are generally exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the supplier or its customs representative can substantiate exportation and exit from the EU customs territory through an accepted customs export record and supporting commercial and transport evidence. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies invoicing, recapitulative-statement, and transport-proof requirements. B2B services supplied to a business established outside France are generally governed by the place-of-supply rule and may be outside the scope of French VAT rather than technically zero-rated; the customer VAT status, place of establishment, contractual evidence, and reverse-charge treatment must be documented. Services directly connected with qualifying exports may qualify for specific exemption rules where the statutory conditions are met. A customs broker must distinguish its own taxable brokerage service from the underlying export of goods and retain evidence supporting the applicable treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration and its Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit or export-results message, such as the electronic confirmation that the goods exited the European Union customs territory
Commercial invoice, sales contract, and packing or shipment records identifying the exporter, consignee, goods, value, and destination
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent transport document
EORI number and customs-representation mandate, including evidence of direct or indirect representation where applicable
Import or destination-country customs evidence where relevant to the transaction
Proof of delivery or other independent transport evidence when required or when the customs exit record is incomplete
VAT invoice showing the legal basis for exemption or reverse charge and the required customer VAT details where applicable
Accounting records, job files, broker instructions, customs correspondence, and payment records sufficient to establish the commercial substance of the transaction

Inward remittance evidence is not a general statutory prerequisite for French export VAT exemption, but payment records may be retained as corroborating evidence and may be relevant to foreign-exchange, anti-money-laundering, or audit procedures
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds applicable to an ordinary French SARL. Export VAT exemption or deduction may be reassessed where the taxpayer cannot prove export, EU exit, customer status, transport, or the actual nature of the service. The reassessment may include unpaid VAT, late-payment interest generally calculated under the applicable French tax rules, and tax penalties. A 10% surcharge may apply to certain late or deficient filings; deliberate breaches may attract a 40% penalty, and fraudulent or abusive conduct may attract an 80% penalty, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Incorrect customs declarations can trigger recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs fines, loss or suspension of customs simplifications, and potentially confiscation or criminal liability. Deliberate VAT fraud may also create criminal exposure. Recovered VAT, interest, and penalties can be assessed retrospectively for the applicable statutory limitation period, commonly three years for ordinary VAT assessments, subject to longer periods or special rules for fraud, concealed activity, or criminal conduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) together with the Direction Générale du Trésor under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, applying the EU Treaty capital-movement liberalisation framework and French Monetary and Financial Code reporting rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates as a euro-area member with fully liberalised current-account and capital-account convertibility under EU law. The euro is freely convertible and the eurozone applies no exchange-control authorisation for profit remittances, dividends, repayment of shareholder loans or liquidation proceeds to non-residents. Regulatory friction arises principally from AML/KYC obligations, financial sanctions screening, French balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds, and for customs brokers the statutory segregation of client funds held for customs duties and taxes. Profit remittance from an SARL is legally unrestricted, but the outgoing payment must be supported by approved minutes, audited/tax-filed accounts, proof of distributable reserves, and banking due diligence evidencing underlying commercial rationale.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in France or the eurozone. Exporters and customs brokers may freely retain euro or foreign-currency proceeds. However, all cross-border fund movements must pass through the banking system and certain flows are reportable to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics, typically when the transaction value exceeds applicable thresholds. For customs brokerage, export proceeds received on behalf of principals must be separately accounted for, must not be mixed with the broker's own funds, and must be remitted to the principal within the agreed settlement timeline without any forced conversion into euro.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus segregated Customs Client Funds Escrow Account (Compte de Fonds Clients Douane)
Operational Account plus Capital Guarantee Escrow Account for customs-bond cover

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Banking
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Cross-border liquidity account, FX execution account and trade settlement account
Operational Account and Treasury/Cash-Pooling Account for group foreign subsidiaries

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for principal treasury and statutory customs client-fund segregation; MEDIUM as a supplementary operational account. Fully digital banking is permissible for payment initiation, but French licensed customs brokers should maintain a Tier-1 bank relationship because DGDDI and AML supervisors expect robust safeguarding of third-party funds. EMIs in France or the EEA holding an electronic-money institution licence under the Second Payment Services Directive may be used for low-value, non-regulated payments, but they are not licensed credit institutions and cannot provide documentary credits, surety bonds, or customs guarantee products. Crossing the statutory thresholds for client-fund custody and treasury concentration mandates movement to a full credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law, particularly Articles L.561-5 and following of the Monetary and Financial Code, imposes enhanced customer due diligence for legal entities. For a newly incorporated SARL with non-resident shareholders or managers, the bank will de facto require the final beneficial owner(s) and the appointed gérant to attend an in-person due-diligence interview at the bank branch or at the company's registered office. Remote onboarding can be accepted only where a prior verified banking relationship exists or where a regulated EU electronic-identity mechanism is used, but the bank retains absolute discretion to call for physical presence. For a DGDDI-licensed customs brokerage house, physical presence should be treated as mandatory and must include presentation of original or certified corporate deeds, the statutory licence, proof of professional liability insurance, and an organisational chart of the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners with complex or opaque corporate chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled certificate of corporate existence for each entity in the ownership chain; certified passport copies of all natural-person beneficial owners; corporate registry extracts with full legal-beneficial-owner registry details; bank reference letters from the foreign parent bank; tax residence certificates; and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the French brokerage operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs broker receiving and disbursing client funds may resemble a money-service activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid DGDDI commissionnaire en douane licence or registered customs representative status; signed customs brokerage mandates or powers of attorney; the AML/CFT policy and risk assessment covering custody of client funds; segregation ledger and bank confirmation that client funds are held in a blocked or designated escrow account; annual audit or certified accountant attestation of fund movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border transactions with trading partners in higher-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening policy referencing EU Regulation No. 269/2014 and national Freezing Act; completed vendor/customer risk questionnaires; underlying commercial invoices and transport documents; certificates of origin and customs declarations; bank-to-bank reference confirmations; and anti-money-laundering training certificates for the compliance officer and gérant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Duty payment accounts showing frequent multi-currency inflows from unrelated third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction file per clearing batch including customs entries, duty assessments, payment confirmations, principal settlement calculations; contractual payroll of account movements; immediate identification of the ultimate beneficiary of each disbursement; and regular reconciliation reports filed with the bank's compliance team.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection into the French SARL must be executed by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer, depending on the remitting jurisdiction. EEA/Eurozone shareholders may use SEPA CT with EUR no-corss-border-fee principles. Non-EEA shareholders must route through SWIFT wire with clear purpose codes, e.g. code 'CAPITAL INJECTION' or the bank-specific equity/loan purpose code. Equity subscriptions must be deposited before registration with Banque des Dépôts et Consignations or a notary where applicable, or evidenced by a certificate of the managing director if the articles so permit. The SARL must report the receipt to Banque de France under the balance-of-payments direct-investment reporting rules where the foreign investment exceeds applicable thresholds. Non-EU direct investments are not screened for a customs brokerage house unless the activity falls within a regulated sensitive sector. Funds must arrive from a banking account in the name of the shareholder; third-party payments require a subordination agreement and source-of-funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing for a customs brokerage house concentrates on settlement of customs duties, taxes, freight forwarders, overseas agents, and trade principals. The primary rails are SWIFT MT103 through the Tier-1 bank for actual remittance, Commercial Letters of Credit (URC 522 or UCP 600) for high-value documentary transactions, and SEPA Credit Transfer for intra-EU payments. Customs duties and import VAT must be debited from the broker's dedicated Customs Duty Account (Compte de Douane) or paid through the fully digital 'Déclaration en Douane' national cashier interface, using the automated Debit at Customs (NAP – Nouvelle Application de Paiement) or the harmonised DGDDI direct-debit system. For every outbound MT103 the broker must state the correct payment purpose, include supporting customs declaration numbers, and ensure that the beneficiary in the end-customer country corresponds exactly to the invoice and shipping documents. International payment must always be preceded by an internal cross-check against the sanctioned-party list and high-risk exposure criteria.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (devis de change à terme) freely deliverable for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF and EUR/CNY exposures
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for restricted or non-fully convertible trade currencies where physical settlement is impractical
FX Swap (swap de change) for simultaneous spot/forward conversion of export proceeds and import disbursement needs
Cross-currency swap (swap de devises) for medium-term matched asset-liability management of the treasury
Currency-linked deposit instruments with embedded forward derivative where permitted under local suitability rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax and results declaration (form 2065-SD with Annexes 2050–2059-G in EDI-TDFC / EFI digital package)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year fiscal period: second business day after 1 May (e.g., 5 May 2025 for FY 2024). Non-calendar fiscal year: second business day after the 4-month post-closing period. Balance of corporate income tax is payable in line with the annual filing obligation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5% if regularized within 30 days of the statutory deadline and 10% thereafter; 40% after a formal notice; 80% for deliberate concealment of activity; late-payment interest of 0.20% per month applies to outstanding corporate income tax.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultats n°2065-SD (Cerfa 12827), with tax annexes n°2050-SD to 2059-SD, filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr — 'Espace Professionnel', mode 'TDFC'/'EFI'.
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of fiscal year end; for calendar-year companies, the deadline is 3 May of the following year (e.g. 2025 return due 3 May 2026); final CIT payment due simultaneously.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN, RNSR (Chamber/Registry), APE/NAF code, address, elected tax regime under CGI art. 206 (I) for SARL, and incorporation date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French branch/entity address; corporate shareholders outside France are treated as non-resident legal persons and must provide their foreign registration identifier in the annex when a permanent establishment is maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting result adjusted by re-integrating non-deductible expenses (luxury cars, fines, excessive interest) and deducting exempt income, tax credits and deficit carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a branch or non-resident owned entity, calculate the French taxable income from the French permanent establishment 'symmetrical' accounts; please file all schedules even if no tax is due because WVTA refund.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss available for carryforward; indicate loss attribution in accordance with CGI art. 209.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a PE in France may carry forward PE-generated losses, but the loss is personal to the French operation and cannot offset foreign-source income of the head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D credit (CIR) and innovation credit (CII) and other refundable credits applied against corporate income tax (IS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits generated by activity in France may be used; excess credits may be refunded in cash under CIR, but foreign-headquartered groups must submit an encrypted file and supporting consistency declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 396 – Contribution sociale sur les bénéfices
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional social contribution on profits and retained earnings above €763,000 (3.3% rate) and / or exceptional surtax if applicable for large groups.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed on the same taxable profit; for non-resident companies, apply if the PE's taxable income exceeds the threshold.
